0.0.n: This country name is the topic of the sentence.

0.1.n: は marks the United States as the topic; the wish comes from Japan, understood from context.

0.3.n: Japanese nouns do not change form to show plural.

0.4.n: を marks tariffs as what will be made higher.

0.5.n: 高い changes to 高く before する to describe making something higher.

0.6.n: With 高く, する expresses raising something's level.

0.7.n: こと turns the preceding action into a noun-like phrase that can be discussed.

0.8.n: について introduces the subject of the thinking: raising tariffs.

0.9.n: 考え方 combines 考える with 方, which expresses a way of doing something.

0.10.n: を marks 考え方 as what Japan wants changed.

0.11.n: The て-form of 変える plus ほしい expresses a wish for someone else to act.

1.0.n: This country name identifies who would raise the tariffs.

1.1.n: が marks the United States as the one doing the action inside the phrase ending in こと.

1.2.n: Here, this noun refers to taxes on imported goods.

1.3.n: を marks tariffs as the thing being raised.

1.4.n: 高く is the form of 高い used before する to express making something higher.

1.5.n: 高くする describes causing something to become higher, rather than simply being high.

1.6.n: こと packages the entire preceding action as a topic that について can introduce.

1.7.n: について links the tariff increase to the statement that follows in the next line.

2.0.n: This is a family name, followed by the person's official title.

2.1.n: 総理 combines with 大臣 to form the title 総理大臣.

2.2.n: 大臣 completes 総理大臣, the Japanese title for the head of government.

2.3.n: が identifies Prime Minister Ishiba as the person who spoke.

2.4.n: This is a family name, followed by the person's official title.

2.5.n: 大統領 follows Trump's name as his title; no さん is needed.

2.6.n: に marks President Trump as the recipient of Ishiba's request.

2.7.n: もう adds the sense of an additional time to 一度.

2.8.n: The て-form of 考える plus ほしい expresses Ishiba's wish for Trump to take action.

2.9.n: と marks the preceding wish as the content of what Ishiba said.

2.10.n: 言いました is the polite past form of 言う.

0.lit: As for America, [Japan] wants [it] to change its way of thinking about making tariffs higher.
0.tip: てほしい expresses wanting someone else to do something; Japan's role as the one wanting is understood from context.

1.lit: Regarding the act of America making tariffs higher,
1.tip: こと turns the whole action into a noun-like phrase, allowing について to mean regarding that action.

2.lit: Prime Minister Ishiba said to President Trump that he wanted him to think once more.
2.tip: と言いました reports the wish before と, so the sentence conveys a request rather than merely describing thoughts.
